title: Research
description: Academy research trees. Research is done at the Academy building (see knowledge/buildings.json) and is split into branches, each with many nodes that cost resources/time and grant permanent bonuses.

entries.name: Economy Research
entries.summary: Economy-focused research branch covering resource output and gathering efficiency upgrades. 44 nodes across 8 tiered families, split into map 'gathering speed' and building 'output/production' upgrades.

gathering_speed.name: Iron Mining
gathering_speed.effect: Speeds up Iron gathering (on the map).

output_production.name: Iron Output
output_production.effect: Improves Iron output at the Ironworks.

output_production.name: Wood Output
output_production.effect: Improves Wood output in the Sawmill.

output_production.name: Bread Output
output_production.effect: Improves Bread output in the Mill.

details.note: 8 families x their tiers = 44 nodes. 'Gathering' = speed of collecting resource nodes on the world map; 'Output' = passive production rate at the city resource buildings.

tier_structure.academy_gating: Tier I starts at Academy Lv.1; each tier raises the requirement up to Academy Lv.30 for the top tiers (V/VI).
tier_structure.prerequisites: Nodes interleave: an Output node unlocks the matching Gathering node, which unlocks the next resource's Output, chaining Bread -> Wood -> Stone -> Iron and back around per tier.

buff_progression.note: Each tier has 3 levels; the buff repeats on levels 1-2 then bumps on level 3. Additive toward the max-tree totals. Gathering buffs are ~2x the size of Output buffs (matching +242.5% vs +119.5% max).

gathering_speed_per_level.note: Food Foraging & Wood Gathering start at +8% (11% L3); Stone Mining & Iron Mining start at +16% (21.5% L3). Higher tiers converge toward +16%/+21.5%.

details.per_node_costs_note: Exact per-level resource/time/power tables are not inlined. Costs scale steeply: Tier I nodes cost thousands and seconds; Tier VI final levels cost ~9M bread and ~11 days each.

entries.name: Growth Research
entries.summary: Growth-focused research branch covering training, healing, and city progression upgrades. 45 nodes across 7 tiered families (six go I-VII, plus Command Tactics I-III).

node_families.name: Bandaging
node_families.effect: Improves healing speed of wounded soldiers.

node_families.name: Camp Expansion
node_families.effect: Boosts the number of troops that can be trained at once (training batch size).

node_families.name: Command Tactics
node_families.effect: Boosts the number of Expedition armies (march queues) that can be deployed at the same time.

details.note: 6 families x 7 tiers + Command Tactics x 3 = 45 nodes. Command Tactics (extra march queues) is the standout — only 3 tiers and high value.

tier_structure.academy_gating: Tier I starts at Academy Lv.1; requirements climb to Academy Lv.30 for Tier VI/VII. The 3rd level of each tier is the big cost/time/buff jump.
tier_structure.prerequisites: Each tier chains: Tooling Up -> Ward + Camp Expansion -> Tool Enhancement -> Bandaging + Trainer Tools -> Command Tactics -> next tier's Tooling Up.

buff_progression.note: Per-tier buff (levels 1-2 repeat, level 3 bumps). Percentages additive; capacity values are flat and additive.

details.per_node_costs_note: Exact per-level resource/time/power tables are not inlined. Costs scale steeply: Tier I nodes cost thousands and seconds; Tier VII final levels cost 18M-23M bread and 116-136 days each (Bandaging VII L3 = ~136 days).

entries.name: Battle Research
entries.summary: Combat research branch (a.k.a. BattleTech). Priority hub for planning upgrades by attack, defense, health, lethality, and deployment capacity.

details.role: Priority hub for combat power planning.

class_terminology.note: Battle Research uses 'Marksman' = Archer and 'Lancer' = Cavalry; Infantry is Infantry. Heroes/troops files use archer/cavalry/infantry.

details.nodes_note: Confirmed mapping from the in-game BattleTech table (buff column is authoritative). 17 node families = 4 all-troops stats + 12 per-class (infantry/archer/cavalry x attack/defense/health/lethality) + 1 deployment capacity. Note some prerequisites reference internal aliases (e.g. 'Skirmishing' = Cavalry-Charge line, 'Marksman Armor' = Leathercraft line, 'Lancer Armor' = Fortified-Mail line, 'Bulwark Foundations' = Bulwark Formations typo).

tier_structure.tiers: Each node family runs through 6 tiers (suffix I..VI). Higher tiers need a higher Academy level and the previous tier.
tier_structure.academy_gating: Tier I starts at Academy Lv.1-8; each tier raises the Academy requirement, up to Academy Lv.30 for Tier VI. The final level of a tier is a big jump in cost/time and buff.
tier_structure.prerequisites: Attack nodes unlock defense -> defense unlocks the all-troops defensive node -> health/lethality -> Regimental Expansion (capacity), which then gates the class lethality/health nodes of the next sub-branch.

buff_progression.note: Per-level buff at max level of each tier (values repeat within a tier, then spike on the tier's last level). Percentages are additive toward the max-tree totals.

details.per_node_costs_note: Exact per-level resource/time/power tables (hundreds of rows) are not inlined here; they live at the source. Costs scale steeply: Tier I nodes cost thousands, Tier VI final levels cost 12M-16M bread each and 80-110 days per level.

default_priority_order.why: Blocked research creates dead time; keep the path open before over-investing in side branches.

default_priority_order.focus: All troop attack and class attack
default_priority_order.why: Attack gives visible combat output and pairs well with troop training and hero upgrades.

default_priority_order.focus: All troop defense and class defense
default_priority_order.why: Defense helps garrisons, rallies, and city protection survive longer under pressure.
Usually one of the best durability stats once basic attack and defense are not lagging.
Stronger once base attack and survivability are already competitive.
Can change march output but gets expensive enough to plan around events.

priority_by_role.rally_leader: Keep attack, lethality, health, and deployment capacity moving together. A leader with only one inflated stat is easier to counter.
priority_by_role.joiner: Do not overspend on a branch just because it scores in an event. Keep combat research aligned with your best hero and troop role.
priority_by_role.garrison_account: Defense and health deserve more attention, especially if the alliance relies on you to hold banners, facilities, or castle windows.

event_timing: Start long research before an event only if completion lands inside the scoring window.
Save universal speedups until you know whether the event rewards research, construction, or troop training more efficiently.
Pair high-cost BattleTech completions with Strongest Governor, Kingdom of Power, or Armament Competition when possible.
Avoid draining gold on low-impact nodes right before a hero or gear event that needs the same premium resources.

verified_sample_rows.note: Representative verified rows to validate the table format; the full per-level tree (hundreds of rows) is not inlined. Fields: name, level, prerequisite, bread, wood, stone, iron, gold, time (raw), power, buff.

branch_map.primary_value: Baseline attack boost across Infantry, Marksman, and Lancer.
Role-specific attack scaling for Infantry, Marksman, and Lancer.
Improves how specific troop classes survive incoming pressure.
Shared defensive base before deeper health and lethality paths.
High-value durability stat for city, rally, and garrison fights.
Damage conversion stat that matters most after core survivability is stable.
Adds troop deployment capacity and changes rally/garrison output ceilings.
Late branch specialization after the account has enough base stat coverage.

entries.name: Research speed boosts and second tech trees
entries.summary: Ways to raise Academy research speed BEYOND the Tool Enhancement tech, plus notes that some content behaves as a second research tree. Tool Enhancement (Growth tree) is the in-tree research-speed multiplier; several temporary/positional buffs stack on top.

external_research_speed_sources: Holding the Chief Minister position in King's Castle.
The King using the 'Fresh Ideas' skill for the kingdom.
details.timing_rule: Temporary research-speed boosts only apply to projects STARTED while the boost is active — you do NOT get the benefit on already-running projects. Time big research starts to coincide with active boosts.
details.oasis_island_second_tree: Once Fountain reaches Level 10, Oasis Island buildings act as a second tech tree; the same archetype research priorities apply there.
details.armory_accounts: Armory accounts are secondary accounts whose purpose is joining the main account's rallies. They use the exact same research priorities as a rally-joining free-to-play player (see rally.json).
details.rally_joiner_reality: Combat/battle research does NOT affect rallies you JOIN — only the rally leader's stats apply (confirmed in rally.json -> rally-principles). This is the core reason research priority differs by archetype.

open_questions: Full per-level resource/time/power tables for every node are not inlined (only tier-level buff patterns and grand totals are captured). Add them if the bot ever needs exact per-node costs.
